description: ETHOS.GLAES is Forschungszentrum Juelich's Python tool for mapping land eligible for infrastructure such as wind turbines or solar parks. It combines exclusion criteria from GDAL-readable rasters and vectors, with configurable distances, thresholds and spatial resolution. Outputs include eligibility rasters, plots and arrays for subsequent placement or potential calculations. Coverage can be any supplied region; source dates follow the underlying layers, while precomputed criteria are separately available for Europe. MIT source is free and includes worked examples. A limitation is that users must supply appropriate data outside the European example coverage and justify their exclusion thresholds. The maintainers test Linux and warn that other operating systems may produce different results. GLAES supports renewable-infrastructure siting and capacity-planning simulations. It complements GlobalEnergyGIS (platform-globalenergygis), which prepares regional resource inputs. The repository cites the 2018 land-eligibility method paper. No spatial data was downloaded.
